examples.en: Whales live by eating plankton.
There is a lot of plankton in seawater.

examples.ko: 플랑크톤은 너무 작아서 눈에 안 보여요.
examples.en: Plankton is so small that you can't see it.

examples.ko: 플랑크톤이 갑자기 늘면 물 색이 변하기도 해요.
examples.en: If plankton suddenly increases, the water's color can change.
In science class we looked at plankton under a microscope.
Small fish grow up eating plankton.

explain: 식물처럼 광합성을 하는 것은 '식물 플랑크톤', 움직이며 먹이를 먹는 것은 '동물 플랑크톤'이라고 해요. 과학 시간이나 바다, 환경 뉴스에 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: Phytoplankton make nutrients from sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광합성을 하는 플랑크톤을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plankton that photosynthesize.

phrases.en: Small fish eat zooplankton.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이며 먹이를 먹는 플랑크톤이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plankton that move and feed on other organisms.

phrases.en: In spring, plankton increase in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이나 환경에 따라 양이 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount changes with season or environment.

explain_en: The photosynthesizing kind is 식물 플랑크톤, and the kind that moves and feeds is 동물 플랑크톤. It mostly appears in science class and in news about the sea or the environment.

examples.ko: 도로 함몰 사고 때문에 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: The road is blocked because of a road collapse.
Residents were evacuated because of a sudden ground collapse.

examples.ko: 함몰이 일어난 곳 근처에는 가지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't go near the place where the collapse happened.

examples.ko: 시청이 함몰을 막으려고 지하 공사를 점검하고 있어요.
examples.en: City Hall is inspecting underground construction to prevent cave-ins.

examples.ko: 함몰은 비가 많이 온 뒤에 더 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: Cave-ins happen more often after heavy rain.
A safety line has been set up at the collapse site.

explain: 뉴스에서 '도로 함몰', '지반 함몰'처럼 앞에 땅이나 도로를 나타내는 말을 붙여 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '땅이 꺼지다'라고 해요. 동사 '함몰되다'와 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: Because of heavy rain, the road caved in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이나 바닥이 아래로 푹 꺼지는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ground or a surface sinking downward.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 함몰 위험이 있어서 조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: This area has a risk of caving in, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 안내나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in safety notices and news.

phrases.example: 공사장 옆 땅이 꺼져서 길을 막았어요.
phrases.en: The ground next to the construction site sank, so they blocked the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함몰'을 일상 대화에서 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to describe a 'hammol'.

explain_en: Ground or surface caving in (도로 함몰), sinkhole. In the news it usually follows words like road or ground, as in '도로 함몰' and '지반 함몰'. In everyday talk people say '땅이 꺼지다'. Learn it together with the verb '함몰되다'.

t90.ax: Cave-ins happen more often after heavy rain.

examples.en: When the Earth gets warmer, sea levels rise.
The sun is rising above the sea surface.
The height of the sea surface differs slightly from sea to sea.
The news said rising sea levels are a problem.
The boat moves slowly close to the sea surface.

examples.ko: 섬이 해수면보다 낮아서 홍수가 자주 나요.
examples.en: The island is lower than sea level, so floods happen often.

explain: 산 높이를 말할 때는 '해발 1,000미터'처럼 '해발'을 쓰고, 바닷물의 높이 변화를 말할 때는 '해수면'을 써요. 뉴스에서 '해수면 상승'이라는 말로 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 해수면 상승 때문에 섬이 작아지고 있어요.
phrases.en: Because of rising sea levels, the island is getting smaller.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in the news.

phrases.example: 이 도시는 해수면보다 낮아서 물이 잘 차요.
phrases.en: This city is below sea level, so it floods easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅의 높이를 바다와 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing the height of land with the sea.

phrases.en: At low tide, the sea level goes down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷물 높이가 낮아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the water height drops.

explain_en: For the height of a mountain, Korean says 해발 1,000미터. For changes in the height of the sea, it uses 해수면. You hear it often in the news as 해수면 상승.

examples.en: The firewood is burning brightly in the fireplace.

examples.ko: 불길이 활활 번지기 전에 빨리 119에 전화하세요.
examples.en: Call 119 quickly before the fire spreads and blazes up.
When the charcoal blazes up, put the meat on.
The fervor of the cheering blazed in the stadium.

examples.ko: 종이를 던지자 불에 활활 타 버렸어요.
examples.en: When I threw the paper in, it went up in flames.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 불꽃이 더 활활 일어났어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, the flames rose even higher.

explain: 불이 기운차게 크게 타오르는 모양을 말해서 주로 '타다', '타오르다'와 함께 써요. 열정이나 분노가 세게 일어나는 것을 불에 빗대어 말할 때도 있어요. 연기나 김이 조용히 오르는 모양은 '모락모락'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The bonfire blazed all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타다'보다 불이 위로 크게 솟는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger than 타다, giving the feeling of flames rising high.

phrases.en: We built a roaring fire with firewood at the campsite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 크게 일으킬 때 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with making a big fire.

phrases.example: 그는 가슴에 활활 타오르는 열정이 있어요.
phrases.en: He has a blazing passion in his heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열정이나 분노가 센 것을 불에 빗대어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compares strong passion or anger to fire.

explain_en: It describes a fire burning large and vigorously, and mostly goes with '타다' or '타오르다'. It can also compare strong passion or anger to fire. For steam or smoke rising quietly, Koreans say '모락모락'.

t90.ax: When the charcoal blazes up, put the meat on.

examples.ko: 선거 때가 되면 후보자들이 가가호호 찾아다녀요.
examples.en: At election time, candidates go around visiting every house.
Volunteers visited house after house and delivered lunch boxes.
I went door to door to greet my neighbors.

examples.ko: 직원이 가가호호 다니면서 설문 조사를 해요.
examples.en: A staff member goes door to door doing a survey.

examples.ko: 명절 저녁에는 가가호호 불이 환하게 켜져요.
examples.en: On holiday evenings, lights are on brightly in every house.

examples.ko: 신문 배달원이 가가호호 신문을 넣고 가요.
examples.en: The newspaper carrier drops a paper at each house.

explain: '집집마다'와 같은 뜻이지만 한자어라서 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 보여요. 보통 '방문하다', '찾아다니다', '돌다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '집집마다'가 더 쉬워요.

phrases.en: Staff went door to door and did a survey.
phrases.nuance_ko: '찾아가다'와 함께 쓰면 직접 집을 방문하는 모습이 나타나요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 찾아가다, it shows people visiting homes in person.

phrases.en: We handed out flyers door to door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 집마다 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when delivering things to each house.

phrases.en: The lights are on in every house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가가호호'와 같은 뜻인데 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 가가호호 but sounds more natural in conversation.

explain_en: It means the same as '집집마다' (house by house), but as a Chinese-origin word it appears more in news and writing. It usually goes with verbs like '방문하다', '찾아다니다' and '돌다'. In everyday talk, '집집마다' is easier.

examples.en: I went through quarantine at the airport and came out.
Quarantine is strict for fruit brought in from abroad.

examples.ko: 검역 때문에 입국이 한 시간 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: Entry was delayed by an hour because of quarantine.
If you want to bring a puppy in, you need quarantine documents.
I got stopped at quarantine and threw away the meat I brought.
The quarantine office opens early in the morning.

explain: 공항이나 항구에서 병이나 해충이 들어오지 못하게 사람, 동물, 식물, 식품을 확인하는 일이에요. 일반적인 '검사'보다 전염병을 막는 목적이 분명해요. 보통 '검역을 받다', '검역 서류'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I went through animal quarantine when I entered the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검역을 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the one being inspected.

phrases.en: The fruit passed quarantine and came into the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제없이 검역을 마쳤다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it finished quarantine with no problem.

phrases.en: I submitted the documents at the port quarantine station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검역을 하는 곳을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where quarantine is carried out.

explain_en: It is the check at airports and ports on people, animals, plants and food to keep diseases and pests from coming in. Compared with a general '검사' (inspection), the purpose of stopping infection is clear. It is commonly used as '검역을 받다' or '검역 서류'.

en: to break down; to come to a rupture; to fall through

examples.ko: 노조는 협상이 결렬되면 파업에 들어갈 것이라고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The union said it will go on strike if the negotiations break down.

examples.ko: 양측 모두 협상이 결렬되지 않도록 한발씩 물러섰어요.
examples.en: Both sides each took a step back so the negotiations wouldn't collapse.
I saw the news that the talks finally broke down.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 대화가 또 결렬돼서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried because the dialogue between the two countries broke down again.

examples.ko: 협상이 결렬될까 봐 모두 긴장하고 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is tense, afraid the negotiations will fall through.

examples.ko: 가격 문제로 계약 논의가 결렬되고 말았어요.
examples.en: The contract discussion ended up breaking down over the price.

explain: 협상, 회담, 논의처럼 서로 이야기하던 일이 합의를 보지 못하고 깨질 때 써요. 사람이 주어가 아니라 '협상이', '회담이'가 주어예요. 반대말은 '타결되다'(합의가 이루어져 마무리되다)예요.

phrases.en: The talks broke down yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 협상이 이미 깨졌다고 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense reports that negotiations have already broken down.

phrases.en: The long negotiation ended in a breakdown.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결국'과 함께 쓰면 합의 없이 끝났다는 결과를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '결국', it stresses that things ended without agreement.

phrases.en: The negotiation fell apart over the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결렬되다'보다 쉬운 말이라 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than '결렬되다', common in conversation.

explain_en: Negotiations or talks end without agreement; formal, news style. Use it when negotiations, talks or discussions fail to reach agreement and fall apart. The subject is the talks themselves, such as '협상이' or '회담이', not a person. The opposite is '타결되다' (to be settled by agreement).

t90.ax: I saw the news that the talks finally broke down.

examples.en: Some companies colluded to raise prices.

examples.ko: 공무원과 결탁해 이득을 챙긴 사람이 붙잡혔어요.
examples.en: A person who colluded with an official and made a profit was caught.

examples.ko: 심판과 결탁하는 일은 스포츠에서 절대 있어선 안 돼요.
examples.en: Colluding with a referee must never happen in sports.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 결탁했다는 소문이 돌고 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that the two companies colluded.

examples.ko: 그 사람들이 결탁하면 시장이 불공정해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If those people collude, the market can become unfair.
We have to find out who they colluded with.

explain: '~와/과 결탁하다'처럼 같이 하는 상대를 함께 말해요. 나쁜 일을 위해 몰래 손잡는다는 뜻이라 '손잡다'나 '협력하다'와 달리 늘 부정적이고, 구어로는 '짜고 하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 직원이 외부 사람과 결탁해서 돈을 빼돌렸어요.
phrases.en: An employee colluded with an outsider and siphoned off money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일의 방법이나 이유를 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link the way or reason of a wrongdoing.

phrases.en: There are rumors that the two companies colluded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실인지 모르는 이야기를 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to pass along an unconfirmed story.

phrases.en: A few merchants conspired to raise the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결탁하다'보다 말투가 편한 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual way to say the same thing.

explain_en: It is used with a partner, as in '~와/과 결탁하다'. Since it means secretly teaming up for something bad, it is always negative, unlike '손잡다' or '협력하다', and in casual speech people also say '짜고 하다'.

examples.en: The trial hearing opens tomorrow morning.
A witness spoke at the hearing.
The hearing date was postponed by a month.
The lawyer is preparing for the hearing.

examples.ko: 공판은 많은 사람이 볼 수 있는 법정에서 열려요.
examples.en: A public hearing is held in a courtroom that many people can watch.
The news reported on the first hearing.

explain: '재판'은 법원이 판단하는 일 전체이고, '공판'은 그중 법정에서 공개로 주장을 듣고 증거를 확인하는 단계예요. 뉴스에서 '첫 공판', '공판이 열리다'로 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 보통 '재판'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The first hearing is held next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 아주 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that appears often in the news.

phrases.en: The hearing date has been set.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판이 열리는 날을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the day the trial is held.

phrases.en: The defendant attended the hearing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법정에 직접 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means appearing in person at court.

explain_en: A specific public hearing session in court, formal legal and news term. '재판' is the whole judging process by a court; '공판' is the stage in open court where arguments are heard and evidence checked. In the news you see '첫 공판' and '공판이 열리다'; in everyday talk people just say '재판'.

en: to engage in a battle; to fight

examples.ko: 두 부대가 산에서 사흘 동안 교전했어요.
examples.en: The two units fought in the mountains for three days.
The soldiers withdrew slowly while engaging the enemy.

examples.ko: 교전하는 지역에서는 전화도 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: In areas where fighting is going on, even phone calls hardly work.

examples.ko: 양쪽이 교전할 때 민간인이 가장 많이 다쳐요.
examples.en: Civilians get hurt most when both sides fight.

examples.ko: 영화 속 군인들이 밤새 교전하고 있어요.
examples.en: The soldiers in the movie are fighting all night.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오랫동안 이웃 나라와 교전해 왔어요.
examples.en: That country has been fighting its neighbor for a long time.

explain: '싸우다'는 사람끼리 일상에서 두루 쓰지만 '교전하다'는 군대나 무장한 쪽이 서로 싸울 때만 써요. 보통 '~와 교전하다'처럼 상대를 같이 말해요.

phrases.example: 두 나라 군대가 지금도 교전하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two countries' armies are still fighting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'로 아직 싸움이 계속되는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-고 있다' describes a battle that is still going on.

phrases.en: The patrol engaged with the rebels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸운 상대를 '~와/과'로 함께 말하는 가장 기본적인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pattern, naming the opponent with '~와/과'.

phrases.example: 양쪽 군대는 교전하지 않고 협상을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: Both armies began negotiations without fighting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형은 싸우지 않고 넘어갔다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means they avoided armed fighting.

explain_en: 싸우다 is the everyday word for fighting between anyone, but 교전하다 is only for armies or armed groups fighting each other. It usually comes with the opponent, like ~와 교전하다.

examples.ko: 정부는 피해 지역에 구호품을 신속히 보내겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government said it would quickly send relief supplies to the affected area.
Our class packed boxes of relief supplies.
When the relief supplies arrived, the residents lined up.
Relief supplies like blankets and bottled water are needed.
We loaded the relief supplies collected by citizens onto a truck.

examples.ko: 구호품 배송이 길 때문에 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The delivery of relief supplies is delayed because of the roads.

explain: 재난이나 가난으로 힘든 사람들에게 보내는 물건이에요. 돈은 '성금'이나 '기부금', 물건은 '구호품'이라고 구별해요. 뉴스에서 '구호품을 전달하다', '구호품을 지급하다'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Volunteers delivered the relief supplies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 직접 건네줄 때 쓰는 뉴스 같은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for handing over supplies.

phrases.en: The relief goods arrived this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구호품'과 같은 뜻이고 띄어 써서 조금 더 풀어 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 구호품, written as two words and sounding a bit more spelled out.

phrases.en: Relief supplies are short, so people are waiting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난 지역의 상황을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the situation in a disaster area.

explain_en: These are goods sent to people suffering from disaster or poverty. Money is '성금' or '기부금', while goods are '구호품'. In the news you often see '구호품을 전달하다' and '구호품을 지급하다'.

t90.ax: Our class packed boxes of relief supplies.

examples.ko: 서울 외곽에는 그린벨트로 묶인 지역이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many areas on the outskirts of Seoul designated as greenbelt.

examples.ko: 그린벨트에서는 건물을 마음대로 지을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't build buildings freely in a greenbelt.
The government announced it would lift part of the greenbelt.

examples.ko: 그린벨트 덕분에 도시 주변에 숲이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the greenbelt, forests remain around the city.
If the greenbelt is lifted, will housing prices rise?
A walking trail has been built in the greenbelt in front of my house.

explain: 공식 이름은 '개발제한구역'이지만 뉴스와 일상에서는 '그린벨트'라고 더 많이 말해요. '그린벨트 해제'처럼 집값이나 부동산 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 땅은 개발제한구역이라 집을 지을 수 없어요.
phrases.en: That land is a development-restricted zone, so you can't build a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그린벨트의 공식 이름이라 서류나 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official name of the greenbelt, used in documents and news.

phrases.example: 정부가 일부 지역의 그린벨트 해제를 발표했어요.
phrases.en: The government announced the release of the greenbelt in some areas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부동산이나 집값 뉴스에 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in real estate and housing news.

phrases.example: 그린벨트 지역은 자연이 잘 보존돼 있어요.
phrases.en: The greenbelt area has well-preserved nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그린벨트로 정해진 곳을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an area designated as a greenbelt.

explain_en: The official term is '개발제한구역', but in news and daily talk people more often say '그린벨트'. It often comes up in housing and real-estate talk, as in '그린벨트 해제'.

examples.en: That disease has been wiped out in this region.
Violence is not easily stamped out.
I hope illegal ads get stamped out.

examples.ko: 범죄가 근절될 때까지 우리는 노력할 거예요.
examples.en: We will keep trying until crime is eliminated.

examples.ko: 오래된 나쁜 습관이 근절돼서 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The old bad habit was eliminated, and everyone was glad.

examples.ko: 사람이 걸리는 병 중에 완전히 근절된 병은 천연두뿐이에요.
examples.en: Smallpox is the only human disease that has been completely eradicated.

explain: '근절되다'는 누가 없앴는지보다 없어진 결과를 말해요. '근절되지 않다', '근절되기 어렵다'처럼 부정으로도 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '없어지다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Drunk driving has still not been eradicated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 계속 남아 있다고 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say a bad thing persists.

phrases.example: 그 병은 백신 덕분에 완전히 근절됐어요.
phrases.en: That disease was completely eradicated thanks to the vaccine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'를 붙여 뿌리까지 없어졌다고 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Completely' stresses that it was wiped out entirely.

phrases.en: Problems like this are hard to eradicate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 없애기 힘든 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for problems that are hard to get rid of.

explain_en: Passive; a bad practice has almost disappeared. 근절되다 focuses on the result of something disappearing, not on who removed it. It often appears in the negative, as in '근절되지 않다' and '근절되기 어렵다'. In daily talk 없어지다 is more common.

en: to prosecute; to indict; to charge

examples.ko: 검사가 그 사람을 사기 혐의로 기소했어요.
examples.en: The prosecutor indicted him on fraud charges.
I heard they decided to prosecute because the evidence was enough.
The prosecution plans to indict three people.
The case in which the company was prosecuted was on the news.

examples.ko: 피해자가 원하지 않아도 기소하는 경우가 있어요.
examples.en: There are cases where they prosecute even if the victim doesn't want it.
The prosecutor gathers evidence in order to indict.

explain: 주어는 거의 항상 '검사'나 '검찰'이에요. 일반 사람이 고소하는 건 '고소하다'이고, 검사가 재판에 넘기는 건 '기소하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스에서 들려요.

phrases.en: The prosecutor sent that person to trial.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기소하다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way to say 기소하다.

phrases.example: 검찰은 다음 주에 그를 기소할 거예요.
phrases.en: The prosecution will indict him next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 일을 말할 때 쓰는 미래형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future form for talking about what will happen.

phrases.en: The prosecutor did not indict that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판에 넘기지 않기로 했을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when it was decided not to bring charges.

explain_en: The subject is almost always a prosecutor. A private person filing a complaint is '고소하다', while a prosecutor taking the case to court is '기소하다'. Rare in daily talk, common in news.

examples.en: The police were dispatched urgently after receiving the report.
Something urgent came up that I needed to contact you about, so I called.
This document has to be handled urgently.
They rushed the patient to the hospital.

examples.ko: 긴급히 필요한 물건이 있으면 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: If there's anything you urgently need, please tell me.
The company is urgently looking for someone.

explain: '급히'와 비슷한데 '긴급히'가 더 격식 있고 뉴스나 공지에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '급하게'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I went to the hospital in a hurry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긴급히'보다 덜 딱딱하고 일상에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than 긴급히 and fine in daily talk.

phrases.en: I left in a rush and forgot my wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural option in everyday talk.

phrases.en: We urgently announced the news of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공지나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 격식 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase common in notices and news.

explain_en: Emergency situations like illness or accidents (긴급히 연락하다) It is similar to '급히', but '긴급히' is more formal and appears often in news and announcements. In everyday conversation people use '급하게' more.

t90.ax: They rushed the patient to the hospital.
